Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we all have the same context: 

What we heard:
- Primary concern: ensuring PII (SSNs, account numbers, customer identifiers) and auth headers are never stored in logs or persisted in a way that is searchable.
- Audit/retention: you need 12 months retention for audit trails but want the ability to retain only metadata for 90 days while purging sensitive payloads earlier.
- Trace IDs & headers: you’d like trace IDs available for debugging but not to be linkable to customer-identifiable data.
- Data residency: production traffic must remain within us-east-1 and any logs that leave the region must be redacted or hashed.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short example redaction config (attached) and a SOC2 excerpt showing our logging controls.
2) Technical deep-dive with our SE (Dev) and our infra lead (Vivek) to show default behavior and per-route redaction capabilities. Can we schedule 45 minutes next week?
3) For procurement/legal: if you want, I can share a short mutual action plan and timeline for enabling the controls.

Please reply with any corrections or priority items; I’ll loop in the right people once you confirm.

Thanks,

> I’m attaching a short example config (redaction-config-example.yaml) and a SOC2 logging-controls excerpt. Dev, Vivek - can you add any technical detail for Alex on request/response logging defaults and regex-based payload redaction?

Hi Alex / Priya - quick technical notes / examples so you know what to expect from our runtime out of the box and what we can customize: 

Default behavior (production):
- Request/response bodies: NOT persisted to long-term logs by default. We keep short-lived in-memory buffers for inference but do NOT write full request bodies to disk unless explicitly enabled per-route.
- Headers: Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-API-Key are redacted by default in any persisted logs.
- Trace IDs: we emit trace IDs for request correlation but store only a salted-hashed token in logs (sha256(traceId + tenantSalt)) by default; original plaintext traceId is ephemeral and not written.
- Metadata: non-sensitive metadata (route, model, latency, top-level status codes) is retained per your retention policy.

Config examples (from redaction-config-example.yaml):
- redaction.enabled: true
- redaction.headers: [Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-API-Key]
- redaction.payload_regexes: ["\\b\\d{3}-\\d{2}-\\d{4}\\b", "\\b\\d{12,19}\\b"]  # SSN-like and long numeric sequences (account numbers)
- trace.storage: hashed
- trace.hash_salt: ${TENANT_SALT}  # per-tenant secret
- retention.payload_days: 7
- retention.metadata_days: 365
- retention.region_restrictions: {us-east-1: true, eu-west-1: false}

Notes / options we can offer for FintechCo: 
- Ingestion redaction: we can run the redaction transformers in the ingress path so raw payloads never touch persistent storage. We also support a mode that writes encrypted blobs to a KMS-bound store, with keys rotated and access audited, if you need temporary access for debugging.
- Trace IDs: if you prefer, we can return a short-lived debug token to your SRE on request (time-limited) instead of storing any derivative on our side.
- Per-route overrides: you can opt-in specific routes to higher fidelity logging (e.g., debug routes) but those require explicit approval and audit logging.

Happy to demo these in the call - if you give us two available windows next week we’ll schedule.
